title: Kashishvara Pandita
html:
The Lord's Mighty Servant

When Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu went in Nilachala to see Jagannatha, Kashishvara walked ahead of Him, parting the crowd — a disciple of Ishvara Puri, a brahmachari, whom Krishnadasa Kaviraja calls “the mighty.” Behind, carrying a water pot, walked his godbrother Govinda. So these two, sent to the Lord by their guru, served Him day after day. Later Mahaprabhu sent Kashishvara to Vrindavana and gave him to take along His very Self — the Deity of Gaura-Govinda; Kashishvara installed Him beside Sri Govindadeva.

The primary sources call him by various names. In the “Charitamrita” he is “Brahmachari Kashishvara” (Adi 10.138), “Kashishvara Gosani” (Madhya 10.185; Adi 8.66) and “the mighty Kashi” (kashi-balavan, Adi 10.142); in Vrindavana Dasa he is “Kashishvara Pandita” (CB, Antya 8.57); in Murari Gupta and in the “Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika” (166), “Sri Kashishvara Gosvami”; in the “Bhakti-ratnakara,” “Kashishvara Pandita” and “Kashishvara Gosvami”; in the “Prema-vilasa,” “Kashishvara Pandita”; in Devakinandana's vandana, “Kashishvara Gosani.” The biographies call him Sri Kashishvara Pandita, Brahmachari Kashishvara Pandita, and also “the mighty” Srila Kashishvara Gosvami Prabhu.1

Kashishvara, the Lord's servant in Puri, and Kashishvara Gosani (Gosvami) of Vrindavana, the teacher of Govinda Gosani, are one and the same person. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati states this plainly in the “Anubhashya” on CC, Adi 8.66: “Sri Kashishvara (Pandita) Gosvami is a disciple of Sri Ishvara Puri,” and there describes his family, birthplace, Deities and service to the Lord in Puri. So too the “Bhakti-ratnakara,” which tells how the Lord sent him from Puri to Vrindavana, and the “Prema-vilasa”: “In the land of Mathura, Kashishvara Pandita is renowned… he is a disciple of Ishvara Puri.” The word “brahmachari” speaks of his ashrama, not of another person.2

Bhringara

Who he is in Krishna's eternal pastimes, Kavi Karnapura tells us:

“The two servants in Vrindavana, Bhringara and Bhangura, were born as the Lord's servants Sri Kashishvara and Govinda.” (“Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika” 137)

By the order of the names Kashishvara is Bhringara and Govinda is Bhangura; so Srila Bhaktisiddhanta understands the verse in the “Anubhashya” (on Adi 8.66 and 10.138), and so do the biographies. Bhringara is one of Krishna's serving boys (cheta) in Vraja. The eternal servant of Krishna came into Gaura's pastimes to serve Him here as well, and in that service his extraordinary strength found its use.3

Elsewhere in the same list Karnapura writes: “Sri Kashishvara Gosvami is the former Shashirekha in Vraja” (“Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika” 166). One of the biographies gives this as the opinion of some, while Srila Bhaktisiddhanta, comparing the two verses, writes with caution: he who in Vrindavana served Krishna as Bhringara, or she who was Shashirekha, is Kashishvara in Gaura's avatara — and adds a question mark. The “Prema-vilasa” (18.27–28) names him and Krishnadasa — apparently Krishna Pandita — as the manjaris Keli-kala and Kunkuma. We follow verse 137.4

Family and Birthplace

Kashishvara's shripata is the village of Chatra (Chatara) in the Hooghly district, a mile from Shrirampur station. His father, Sri Vasudeva Bhattacharya, was a brahmana of the Kanjilal Kanu family, of the Vatsya gotra.5 The family bore the hereditary title “Chaudhuri,” and therefore the part of Chatra where Kashishvara's temple stands is called Chaudhuripara. All this Srila Bhaktisiddhanta records in the “Anubhashya” on CC, Adi 8.66.

That Kashishvara came from Bengal, Mahaprabhu Himself says. In Nilachala, naming His Bengali devotees to Vallabha Bhatta, He said:

“Acharyaratna, Acharyanidhi, Gadadhara Pandita, Jagadananda, Damodara, Shankara, Vakreshvara, Kashishvara, Mukunda, Vasudeva, Murari and all the other devotees who descended in Gauda have preached the name of Krishna and prema throughout the world, and whatever devotion to Krishna I have, I have gained in their company.” (CC, Antya 7.48–50)

Murari Gupta, too, opens with his name the list of “residents of Gauda” who came to Nilachala (4.1.4).

His sister's son was Sri Rudra (Rudrarama) Pandita of Vallabhapura. Vallabhapura lies a mile north of Mahesha; there Rudra Pandita installed the Deity of Sri Radha-vallabha. The “Charitamrita” names him a twig of Shankararanya's branch (Adi 10.106), and Karnapura writes: “Krishnachandra's friend in Vraja named Varuthapa is Rudra Pandita, dear to Gauranga” (“Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika” 135).

The service of Kashishvara's Deities in Chatra was carried on by his brother's descendants. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta writes that in his day the manager was Sri Shivachandra Chaudhuri of that family; nine seers of rice were allotted daily for the service; the lands long set aside for the Deities the brother's descendants had lost in the courts, and the service had fallen into decline. One of the biographies, quoting another's commentary, says on the contrary that the Deities have land enough.6

The Deities of Chatra

In the temple in Chaudhuripara reside the Deities of Sri Gauranga and Sri Radha-Govinda installed by Kashishvara Pandita. Every year Dola-yatra — Dol-purnima — is celebrated there.

One of the biographies, citing the commentary of Srila Bhaktivedanta Swami Maharaja on CC, Adi 8.66, adds that Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati visited this temple; that the commentator himself, while still a householder, went there and took prasada; that the Deities of Radha-Govinda and Gauranga are extraordinarily beautiful; and that a temple of Jagannatha stands nearby.

Disciple of Ishvara Puri

Kashishvara took shelter of Sri Ishvara Puri — whom the Lord chose as His guru — and remained a brahmachari. Govinda served Ishvara Puri together with him. Krishnadasa Kaviraja writes, listing the branches of the Chaitanya tree:

“Brahmachari Kashishvara was a disciple of Ishvara Puri, and Sri Govinda was his dear follower. At the time of his departure both received his order, came to Nilachala and met the Lord.” (CC, Adi 10.138–139)7

Both served their guru as long as he remained in this world, and Kashishvara was blessed with his abundant mercy. Before his departure Ishvara Puri told them: when he was gone, they should go to Nilachala and serve Sri Chaitanya Himself. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura writes the same in the “Amrita-pravaha-bhashya”: on their guru's order they came to Mahaprabhu in Nilachala. The “Prema-vilasa” says that Ishvara Puri entrusted Kashishvara to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, and the Lord wove him into His tree as one of its chief branches (18.13–14).

Coming to the Lord

Govinda went to the Lord at once and reached Puri when Mahaprabhu had already returned from His journey through South India. Introducing himself, he said:

“I am the servant of Ishvara Puri, and my name is Govinda. On Puri Gosani's order I have come to You. At the time of his passing, Gosani ordered me, ‘Go to Krishna Chaitanya and serve Him.’ Kashishvara will come after visiting all the holy places, but on my master's order I have hurried to Your feet.” (CC, Madhya 10.132–134)

Kashishvara first went round the holy places — according to one of the biographies, he travelled all over India — and came later.8 In the same account the “Charitamrita” says:

“The next day Kashishvara Gosani came, and the Lord received him with honour and kept him with Himself. He would take the Lord for the darshana of Jagannatha, walking ahead and keeping back the crowds.” (CC, Madhya 10.185–186)

In the summary of the pastimes at the beginning of the Madhya-lila, too, Kaviraja mentions his coming: “Paramananda Puri, Govinda and Kashishvara arrived” (Madhya 1.129).

To accept their service was not simple for the Lord, and He Himself disclosed His difficulty to Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya:

“The Lord said, ‘Bhattacharya, consider this: My guru's servant is worthy of My respect. It is not proper for Me to have him serve Me, yet My guru has ordered it. What am I to do?’ The Bhatta said, ‘The guru's order is mighty, and one must not transgress it. Scripture bears witness to this.’” (CC, Madhya 10.142–144)

And Sarvabhauma gave two examples. Lakshmana, knowing that Parashurama on his father's order had stopped short of nothing, accepted his elder brother's will, for the orders of the guru and of elders are carried out without deliberation (“Raghuvamsha” 14.46); and Sri Rama Himself says that He will carry out His guru's order without deliberation: in this lies Sita's good, and His own above all (“Ramayana,” Ayodhya-kanda 22.9).

Then the Lord accepted both disciples of His guru:

“Out of regard for their connection with His Guru, the Lord honoured them both, yet in obedience to the Guru's order He gave them His service.” (CC, Adi 10.140)

One of the biographies says: the Lord honoured them as His equals and yet, on His guru's order, made them His personal servants. The Lord Himself, the Master of all, needs no one's service; He accepted a guru in His lila and accepted the service of His guru's disciples out of mercy — to Ishvara Puri, whose wish He fulfilled, and to them. So Mahaprabhu taught the world a lesson in obedience to the guru: all that is connected with the guru is worthy of honour, and the guru's word is not debated.

Ahead of the Lord

To each of the two servants the Lord gave his own service:

“The Lord gave Govinda the service of His person, and when He went to see Jagannatha, Kashishvara walked ahead of Him. Through the dense crowd the Lord passed untouched, for the mighty Kashishvara pushed the people aside and cleared the way.” (CC, Adi 10.141–142)

Kashishvara was very strong. But the strength of the eternal servant Bhringara is no worldly might; it is a gift for service. He was not guarding some “important person”: he was protecting the Lord, whose body the crowd was not to touch. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta puts this into a subheading of the “Anubhashya” on Madhya 10.186: “The mighty Kashishvara puts his strength to good use in the service of the Lord.” A Vaishnava's strength is precious only because it is given to the Lord.

So it was day after day. Describing how, after the cleansing of the Gundicha temple, the Lord went with all the devotees to see Jagannatha, Kaviraja paints the same picture:

“Happily Mahaprabhu took all the devotees and went to see Jagannatha. Kashishvara went in front, holding back the crowd, and behind came Govinda, carrying a water pot.” (CC, Madhya 12.206–207)9

So too Kavi Karnapura sees the Lord's procession in the drama “Chaitanya-chandrodaya”: “Ahead, Kashishvara, parting the throngs of people; behind, Govinda, guarding His playful gait; on either side, Puri-ishvara and Svarupa — so will Gaurachandra go to the festival of the eyes” (10.41). One of the biographies says that Kashishvara was given the duty of shielding the Lord from the crowd.

At the Ratha-yatra, when the Lord danced before Jagannatha's chariot, three rings of devotees surrounded Him:

“Three circles were formed to hold back the crowd. In the first stood mighty Nityananda. Kashishvara, Mukunda and all the other devotees joined hands and formed the second ring. Outside them, Prataparudra and his officers formed a circle and held back the crowd.” (CC, Madhya 13.88–90)10

Serving Prasada

Another service of Kashishvara's was distributing mahaprasada to the Vaishnavas. When the Lord and the devotees had cleansed the Gundicha temple, Mahaprabhu held a feast in the garden, and the food was served by seven:

“Svarupa Gosani, Jagadananda, Damodara, Kashishvara, Gopinatha, Vaninatha and Shankara — these seven served the food there, while from time to time the devotees called out ‘Hari!’” (CC, Madhya 12.163–164)11

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta writes that in Purushottama Kashishvara distributed prasada to the devotees after kirtana.

He did the same service on other days. When Vallabha Bhatta fed the Lord and His associates, “Svarupa, Jagadananda, Kashishvara and Shankara served the food, and so did Raghava and Damodara” (CC, Antya 7.66). And at the festival of Haridasa Thakura's departure Mahaprabhu began to serve the feast Himself, but Svarupa begged Him to sit and watch:

“Svarupa said, ‘Lord, sit down and watch. I shall serve with these helpers.’ Svarupa, Jagadananda, Kashishvara and Shankara — these four served without pause.” (CC, Antya 11.83–84)

And he himself, a brahmana, would invite the Lord to a meal. In the days when the devotees vied with one another to invite Mahaprabhu, “Gopinatha Acharya, Jagadananda, Kashishvara, Bhagavan, Ramabhadra Acharya, Shankara and Vakreshvara would from time to time invite Him to rice cooked at home” (CC, Antya 10.154–155).

Beside the Lord in Nilachala

From then on Kashishvara lived with the Lord constantly:

“Gadadhara Pandita Gosani lived in Nilachala, as did Vakreshvara, Damodara, Shankara and Haridasa. Jagadananda, Bhavananda, Govinda, Kashishvara, Paramananda Puri and Svarupa Damodara lived there too.” (CC, Madhya 1.252–253)

And every morning the Lord went with them to see Jagannatha: “With Puri Gosani (Paramananda Puri), Jagadananda, Svarupa Damodara, Damodara Pandita, Govinda and Kashishvara, the Lord stayed at Nilachala, and every morning He went to see Jagannatha” (CC, Madhya 15.184–185).

When Advaita Acharya and the Gauda devotees came from Bengal for the Ratha-yatra, Kashishvara went out with the Lord to meet them. Vrindavana Dasa names him in a long list of those who went: “Kashishvara Pandita, Bhagavan Acharya, Sri Pradyumna Mishra…” (CB, Antya 8.56–61); so does Murari Gupta: “Sri Kashishvara Gosvami and Bhagavan Pandita; Srila Pradyumna Mishra…” (4.17.19).12

At times the Lord's servants ate with Him when He was invited to a meal. Hence, Kaviraja relates, “to invite the Lord for a meal cost four panas of cowries, for sometimes Kashishvara and Govinda ate as well, three persons in all” (CC, Antya 8.38). Srila Bhaktisiddhanta, in a subheading of the “Anubhashya,” calls them here the disciples of Sri Ishvara Puri. And when Ramachandra Puri reproached the Lord for eating much and Mahaprabhu began to eat only half a meal, He took care of His servants:

“The Lord ate half a meal and Govinda half a meal, and then all the devotees gave up eating. The Lord ordered Govinda and Kashishvara, ‘You two beg elsewhere and fill your stomachs.’” (CC, Antya 8.58–59)

Kashishvara went with the Lord when He set out from Orissa towards Vrindavana by way of Gauda (Madhya 16.127–129), and welcomed Him when He returned from Vrindavana to Nilachala (Madhya 25.221). When Sanatana Gosvami came to Puri, the Lord introduced him to His associates, Kashishvara among them (Antya 4.108–110). With Jagadananda, Svarupa, Govinda, Shankara, Damodara and Mukunda he heard by the sea the singing of Junior Haridasa, who had already left his body (Antya 2.153–154). And on the day the Lord fell in ecstasy near Aitota, “Kashishvara, Govinda and the others were elsewhere” (Madhya 13.183).

Krishnadasa Kaviraja glorifies Mahaprabhu as “Him who is dear to Kashishvara” (CC, Antya 11.4). Vrindavana Dasa says of the Lord: “Glory to Him who is dear to the heart of Vakreshvara and Kashishvara!” (CB, Madhya 1.6) — and: “All glory to the life and wealth of Haridasa and Kashishvara!” (CB, Madhya 24.3).13

Other poets, too, see him beside the Lord. In Karnapura's mahakavya “Kashishvara and the others, and Kashi Mishra… and this Govinda… vying with one another, eagerly drink with their eyes the nectar of His dance” (16.33). Murari Gupta calls the Lord “He who gives honour to Kashishvara” (4.18.15) and names Kashishvara among those who, together with Ramananda, Svarupa, Paramananda, Vasudeva and Govinda, served the Lord without cease (4.24.13). In a pada signed by Ramananda the mighty Kashishvara supports Advaita in the Lord's kirtana, and in a pada of Ramachandra Dasa he sings Gaura's glories with Abhirama, Pandita Purushottama and Narahari.

Kashishvara in Navadvipa?

Vrindavana Dasa names Kashishvara among those present in the pastimes of Navadvipa as well: in the kirtanas of the days of the Mahaprakasha (CB, Madhya 8.114), in the list of associates after the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai (13.338), and on the day the Lord came with kirtana to Shridhara and drank water from his iron pot: “Govinda, Govindananda, Shrigarbha, Shriman, Kashishvara, Sri Jagadananda and Rama also wept” (CB, Madhya 23.451). One of the biographies refers these passages to our Kashishvara, recalling also his kirtanas at Shrivasa's house and the bathing in the Ganga. Kavi Karnapura in the “Chaitanya-chandrodaya” names Kashishvara among the Gauda devotees who came to Puri with Advaita, and the Lord greets them: “Kamalananda and Kashishvara, is all well with you?” (act 8). Whether this is the same Kashishvara, the disciple of Ishvara Puri, the sources do not say outright.14

Gaura-Govinda

When Sri Rupa Gosvami revealed Sri Govindadeva in Vrindavana and opened His service, he informed Mahaprabhu by letter. Having read the letter, the Lord could not contain His joy and told Kashishvara to leave Puri without delay for Vrindavana — to Rupa and Sanatana, to help them. The “Bhakti-ratnakara” relates:

“The Lord says to Kashishvara in private: ‘You will have to go to Vrindavana.’” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 2.438)

To leave the Lord was unbearable for Kashishvara:

“Kashishvara says: ‘Prabhu, to leave You — my heart breaks; do what is fitting.’ Gaurahari, understanding Kashishvara's heart, carefully gave him a Deity — His own form. The Lord, together with that Deity, partook of rice and other foods; seeing this, Kashishvara was filled with supreme joy. The Lord gave the name — Sri Gaura-Govinda; with Him Kashishvara came to Vrindavana. Placing the Lord at Sri Govinda's right, he, overwhelmed with prema, performs wondrous service.” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 2.439–443)

The Lord, who dwells in every heart, understood that Kashishvara could not bear separation, and gave him not an image or a keepsake of Himself but His very Self — svarupa-vigraha, His own form. And so that Kashishvara should have no doubt, the Lord ate together with the Deity: Mahaprabhu and Gaura-Govinda are one. So faith was born in Kashishvara; and serving Gaura-Govinda in Vrindavana, he served the Lord in person and was consoled in his separation from Him.15

The “Bhakti-ratnakara” gives another account as well — from the “Sadhana-dipika,” “an account heard from the lips of an associate of Mahaprabhu”:

“Once Sri Mahaprabhu said to Sri Kashishvara: ‘Go to Vrindavana and live near Sri Rupa and Sanatana.’ Hearing this, he was both delighted and astonished. The crest-jewel of the omniscient, Gaura, knowing his heart, said again: ‘Bring the Deity of Sri Krishna that stands beside Jagannatha, and know that I am non-different from Him, Bhagavan Himself; serve Him thus.’ Hearing this, he fell silent. Then Sri Krishna in the form of the Deity and Mahaprabhu ate together. After this Sri Kashishvara, bowing down like a rod, brought the Deity of Gaura-Govinda to Vrindavana. This is the Mahaprabhu beside Sri Govinda.” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 2.444)

And the “Sadhana-dipika” prays: “May Gaura-Govinda be merciful to me, who with the radiance of His feet has conquered Madana, with the radiance of His face has crushed the pride of the lotus and the jewel, and whose feet are Sri Rupa's shelter” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 2.445).

Manohara Dasa's “Anuraga-valli” tells it in its own way. Rupa asked the Lord to send an adhikari, a chief servitor, for Govinda. The Lord went over in His mind all the Gauda devotees in Nilachala and called Kashishvara — “a disciple of Sri Ishvara Puri, most fortunate, one of Mahaprabhu's chief associates” — and told him to go and serve Govinda. He wept: “If for a moment I do not see Your lotus feet, the world seems empty, my eyes go blind.” The Lord smiled and answered: “What I am, that is Govinda — there is no difference at all… here, I give you My very Self,” and placed in his hands a Deity of Gaurasundara: “This is I; you will always have My darshana; whatever service you render I shall accept” (4.70–83). In Vrindavana Rupa and Sanatana, seeing Gauranga, were plunged in prema and received Kashishvara with honour; after the abhisheka the Deity was placed at Govinda's right (4.85–89). Kashishvara served Govinda and offered Him camphor betel, and Rupa made him Govinda's first adhikari. But Kashishvara was always intoxicated with prema, and when he thought of Mahaprabhu's departure he did not know where he was and could not attend to all the details of the service; so Rupa, asking his consent, made Krishna Pandita adhikari of Govinda while Kashishvara was still present (4.91–98).16

In Vrindavana

In Vrindavana Kashishvara lived among the Lord's associates. The “Bhakti-ratnakara” says that Gopala Bhatta lovingly associated “with Lokanatha, Bhugarbha, Kashishvara Pandita,” Paramananda and Krishnadasa (1.202). The “Prema-vilasa” writes: “In the land of Mathura, Kashishvara Pandita is renowned; his devotion to Rupa and Sanatana is very deep” (18.12); it also speaks of his great friendship with Krishnadasa Brahmachari (24.183; 25.822) and tells how Rupa Narayana bowed down “to Brahmachari Krishnadasa and Kashishvara” (19.657).

The highest testimony to him was left by Sri Sanatana Gosvami. In the opening verses of the “Hari-bhakti-vilasa” he prays: “Kashishvara shines in Krishna's forest, and so does Sri Krishnadasa with Lokanatha,” and in the mangalacharana of the “Vaishnava-toshani”: “I praise those dear to Vrindavana, who have taken shelter at Sri Govinda's feet: the illustrious Kashishvara, Lokanatha and Sri Krishnadasa” (as given in the “Bhakti-ratnakara,” 1.321, 1.323). The second verse is also cited in the “Narottama-vilasa” (1.97) and the “Anuraga-valli” (4.129–130).17

Kashishvara's disciple was Govinda Gosani, the servitor of the Deity of Govinda. Krishnadasa Kaviraja, telling which Vaishnavas of Vrindavana bade him write the “Charitamrita,” says:

“Govinda Gosani, the disciple of Kashishvara Gosani, is the dear servant of Govinda, and there is none to equal him.” (CC, Adi 8.66)

One of the biographies calls Govinda Gosvami the pujari of Sri Govinda and adds a second disciple — Yadava Acharya; the “Bhakti-ratnakara,” too, names both (13.323, see below). The “Prema-vilasa” says that Kashishvara had a disciple, a brahmana resident of Vraja named Bhaktakashi, and that Govinda Gosani and Yadava Acharya, two brahmana youths from Gauda, left home and took shelter at his feet (18.23–25; 25.498).18

Departure

According to our calendar, that of the Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math, the day of Srila Kashishvara Pandita's departure is Gaura Chaturdashi of the month of Damodara (in 2026, 23 November), the same day as Bhugarbha Gosvami's; the biographies, too, name the shukla-chaturdashi of the month of Kartika.19 The year of his departure the sources do not give.

He left this world soon after the Lord's disappearance and before Shrinivasa came to Vraja. According to the “Bhakti-ratnakara,” on the way to Vrindavana Shrinivasa heard from brahmanas walking the same road:

“At Nilachala Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the Lord of all, became invisible to everyone's eyes. Hearing that unbearable news, Kashishvara Gosvami disappeared. Raghunatha Bhatta, the reciter of the Bhagavata — in separation from the Lord he too disappeared.” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 4.194–196)

And Shrinivasa wept: “O Sanatana, Rupa, oceans of virtue, Raghunatha Bhatta, Sri Pandita Kashishvara!” (4.214). So too the biographies say that when Shrinivasa came to Vraja he learned that Rupa, Sanatana, Kashishvara and Raghunatha Bhatta had already disappeared.20

The same news reached Narottama. The “Narottama-vilasa” relates that, hearing that Raghunatha, Kashishvara, Rupa and Sanatana had disappeared, he wept, rolling in the dust, and cried out: “Kashishvara Pandita! Sri Bhatta Raghunatha!”; and that night all four appeared to him in a dream and consoled him (2.188–196). It also says that when Kashishvara Gosvami disappeared, Sri Krishna Pandita took up the service of Govinda's feet (2.243).

His samadhi is in Vrindavana. When Shrinivasa, Narottama and Shyamananda took leave of Vrindavana to return to Gauda, they “saw the samadhi of Kashishvara Gosvami and bowed down, rolling in the dust,” and Narahari Chakravarti exclaims: “Who can tell the glory of Kashishvara, who brought Sri Gaura-Govinda to Vrindavana and seated Him at Govinda's right! Seeing the beauty of the Two, the heart overflows. Sri Chaitanya, won over by Sri Kashishvara's love, came in the form of the Sri Vigraha to the western land” (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 6.444–447). He then cites a verse of the “Sadhana-dipika”: “I bow to the illustrious Kashishvara, out of love for whom Chaitanyadeva Himself mercifully came to the western land” (6.448) — and adds: “Kashishvara, dear to the Lord, is known throughout the world; Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana are absorbed in his virtues” (6.449). It was seen also by Ramachandra Kaviraja (9.204) and by Jahnava Ishvari, who, as she left Vrindavana, wept at the samadhis of the four — “Raghunatha Bhatta, Pandita Kashishvara, Gosvami Sri Sanatana and the wise Rupa” (11.257–258).

One of the biographies writes that when Virachandra, Nityananda's son, came to Vrindavana, Jiva, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and others met him on the road, and among them “Kashishvara with his disciples Govinda Gosvami and Yadava Acharya.” This seems to be a reading of the “Bhakti-ratnakara” on Virachandra's welcome: “Kashishvara Gosani, who is known everywhere, with whom Sri Krishna Pandita is in close friendship; the disciples of Kashishvara Gosani, great aryas, Govinda Gosani and Sri Yadavacharya; Govinda, Yadavacharya and all the others went in great joy” (13.322–324). It is the disciples who go to meet him; Kashishvara is named in order to name them: according to the “Bhakti-ratnakara” he had left this world before Shrinivasa came, and Virachandra came later.

But the Lord's eternal associate is never parted from Him. When at Kheturi, at Narottama's great festival, Mahaprabhu appeared with His associates during the kirtana, Kashishvara was among them: “Sanatana, Rupa, Raghunatha, Kashishvara — countless associates of Sri Prabhu danced” (“Narottama-vilasa” 7.121). The “Bhakti-ratnakara,” too, names him among the dancers in that kirtana: “…Jagadisha, Sri Yadunandana, Kashishvara; Sri Raghunatha Bhatta dances, Rupa-Sanatana” (10.595–596).21

In Lists and Vandanas

Kashishvara's name stands in many lists of the Lord's associates. Lochana Dasa names him among those who descended with the Lord (Sutra-khanda 8.628); the “Bhakti-ratnakara” and the “Narottama-vilasa” glorify him in vandanas and lists. The “Vaishnava-vandanas” remember him more than once: the vandana ascribed to Jiva Gosvami names him beside Garuda and Jagadisha and among the Vrindavana devotees; Devakinandana — as “Kashishvara Gosani, especially renowned in Mathura-mandala”; another vandana — as “the wise Kashishvara, whom all call the renowned ‘Bhakta.’” His name is found also in the pada of Narahari that concludes the “Bhakti-ratnakara” — beside Vallabha, Sanatana, Sadashiva and Vishvarupa — and in Shrinivasa's dream of Navadvipa, where he is among the associates surrounding Gaurachandra (“Bhakti-ratnakara” 12.4057).

He is remembered beyond Bengal as well. In the “Bhaktamal” of Nabhadasa (about 1600), among the saints who became “a support for carrying [souls] across the current of worldly existence,” “Kashishvara Avadhuta” is named (96), and Priyadasa (1712) explains: “Sri Gosai Kashishvara was formerly the best of avadhutas; having come to love Nilachala, he lived [there]… Receiving the order of Mahaprabhu Krishna Chaitanya, he came [to Vrindavana]; he saw Vrindavana and loved it with all his heart. He received the right to serve Govinda-chandra, the rasika; he longs only for His lotus face, the life of his life” (398).

Narahari Chakravarti, in the “Namamrita-samudra,” where his prayers call upon the Lord's associates, names him beside Govinda, the Lord's servant:

“Govinda, Garuda, Kavichandra, Kashishvara! Make this fallen one a servant of your servants.” (“Namamrita-samudra” 17)

Significance

Kashishvara Pandita is Krishna's eternal servant Bhringara, who came into Gaura's pastimes together with Govinda. His extraordinary strength was wholly given to service: he walked ahead of the Lord, parting the crowd so that no one should touch Mahaprabhu's body; he served mahaprasada to the Vaishnavas; and he was one of the second ring around the dancing Lord at the Ratha-yatra. A Vaishnava's strength is of value only in that it serves the Lord.

In his coming to the Lord, Mahaprabhu showed how to honour the guru: He accepted His guru's servants, whom He revered as elders, only because His guru had so ordered, for the guru's word is not debated.

And in sending him to Vrindavana the Lord revealed that He and His Deity are one. Seeing that Kashishvara could not bear separation, the Lord gave him His very Self in the form of Gaura-Govinda and ate together with Him. Kashishvara placed Gaura-Govinda at Sri Govindadeva's right and, serving Him, served the Lord in person.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta recognises him as the disciple of Ishvara Puri and the teacher of Govinda Gosani, and the biographies call Kashishvara's glory boundless.
